Title: Sacrorum conciliorum nova, et amplissima collectio ... quae Joannes Dominicus Mansi evulgavit. Tomus vicesimus septimus: ab anno MCCCCIX usque ad annum MCCCCXVIII
Creator: Giovanni Domenico Mansi (ed.), after Philippe Labbe, Gabriel Cossart and Nicolas Coleti
Publisher: Facsimile reproduction for H. Welter, Paris, of the Venice edition of 1784 (original: Antonio Zatta, Venice)
Publication Date: 1902
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page reads 'TOMUS VICESIMUS SEPTIMUS ... VENETIIS MDCCLXXXIV' and '(Editio iterata ad Editionis principis exemplum ab Huberto Welter Bibliopola ... Parisiis MDCCCCII...)' in the OCR (the last numeral is read with a stray letter, 'MDCCCCIID'); the underlying edition is of 1784; the item record carries no rights field.
Language: lat (the Latin acts of the Councils of Pisa and Constance; the long s is read as f)
Source: Internet Archive item sacrorumconcilio0027joan (archive.org/details/sacrorumconcilio0027joan), full-text file sacrorumconcilio0027joan_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged apart from this header. Nothing stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped. Latin sampled at opening, middle and end: the long s is read as f throughout; otherwise readable with scattered errors. The first pages are stamp noise. A second witness for exact wording until checked against the page images. This file is 4.7 MB, over the 3 MB limit for second witnesses, and is vendored under the exception for a council's core acts with no smaller edition.
Content note: Mansi tomus 27, 1409 to 1418: the Council of Pisa (1409) with its additions and appendix, and the Council of Constance from its first session, with the proceedings against Wyclif and Jerome of Prague (the citation of Jerome is printed in it) and, by the standard Mansi citation, the decree on the council's authority (session V, col. 585) and the decree 'Frequens' (session XXXIX, col. 1159); the closing sessions print the decree on councils at fixed intervals. The condemnation of Hus is in the same sessions. The conciliar decrees themselves. Finke's volumes 2 and 3 are the better edited witness for the diaries; this volume carries the decrees as printed in the canonical collection.
